thread:
lara: Quick bench update — seeing p99 spikes in eu-west when routing from edge pop in london. Did a run across A100/H100 + int8/float16. Sharing logs.

mike: can you paste numbers? p50/p95/p99?

lara: Short table:
- us-east-1 (A100, fp16): p50 28ms, p95 110ms, p99 240ms
- us-west-2 (H100, fp16): p50 22ms, p95 95ms, p99 300ms
- eu-west-1 (A100, int8): p50 35ms, p95 150ms, p99 520ms

sanjay: eu p99 520ms is wild. is that kv cache cold or routing to warm pop?

lara: Good q. I forced cache warm and re-ran — p99 dropped to ~260ms but still worse than us regions.

nina: Could be kernel selection fallback on int8. We saw a slow kernel path for long seqs on older cuDNN combos.

mike: Chunk of requests from london pop get routed to eu-west by edge policy; traffic sometimes goes across -> added network hop.

lara: Repro command I used:
```bash
ri bench run --model redwood-2-large --seq 2048 --batch 4 \
  --regions us-east-1,us-west-2,eu-west-1 \
  --gpus a100,h100,a100 --quant fp16,int8,fp16 --duration 600
```
Output snippet:
```
[eu-west-1][int8] p50=35ms p95=150ms p99=520ms qps=190
[us-west-2][fp16] p50=22ms p95=95ms p99=300ms qps=310
```

sanjay: If kernel fallback is the issue, we should pin kernel version on eu-west pool to the optimized fused-kernel build and re-run.

nina: Also sizing note — to hit 99th SLAs we need higher reserved slots in eu-west due to routing variance. Current dedicated pool at 40 slots saturates at 350 qps; need ~55 for buffer.

mike: Agreed. Policy action: change edge routing preference for london pop to prefer us-west when eu-west latency > 120ms for p95 window.

lara: I can try two experiments:
1) Force fused kernels on eu-west and run bench
2) Set edge rule to prefer us-west and measure p99 reduction

eval-bot: new eval run queued: job id eb-17855-1 (expected ~12m)

ops-bot: deploy: kernel-pin-eu-west -> production (canary 10%) at 1785554400

mike: After canary results (10%) we'll scale to 50% if p99 improves >30%.

lara: Early canary quick numbers: p99 in eu-west dropped from 520ms -> 270ms on pinned kernel. qps steady.

nina: Good sign. Next check quantization regression on outputs — run evals on prompt set.

lara: Running evals now; will share diff. initial quality delta (int8 vs fp16) looks within threshold for 95% prompts.

mike: OK let's roll kernel pin to full pool and add reserved slots to match capacity sizing.

sanjay: I'll update routing config and capacity request ticket. tagging @infra and @platform for follow-up.

lara: Thanks — follow-up: https://console.redwood/internal/bench/1785554321 (dashboard)

mike: :thumbsup:
